headline: Real product, real churn problem: you're filling a bucket with a 9% hole in it.
thesis: PawClaim has genuine pull — 68% week-12 retention on clinics is not nothing, and a domain founder who ran vet ops is the right person to be here. But 9% monthly logo churn against 11% MoM growth means you are running to stand still, and at $22k burn on 7 months of runway you do not have the time to out-grow it. Fix retention and this is a seed round. Don't, and the next conversation is a bridge.

categories.verdict: Growing, but churn is eating it
categories.reasoning: $14k MRR at 11% MoM is a real business forming, but 9% monthly logo churn means net growth is roughly 2%. With $22k burn and 7 months of runway, you are one bad quarter from a bridge you don't want.
A backend engineer from Square paired with someone who ran ops at two vet chains is textbook founder-market fit, and both full-time. This is the category doing the heaviest lifting in your favour.

categories.verdict: Pull exists, retention curve doesn't flatten
categories.reasoning: 68% at week 12 is decent for vertical SaaS and NPS 41 across 30 responses is a real signal. But the curve is still sloping at week 12, which is the difference between a painkiller and a well-liked vitamin.

Your bottom-up $110M is honest, which already puts you ahead of most decks. The three practice-management integrations are the beginnings of a moat, but integrations get copied — what's defensible is the claims data you'll sit on, and you didn't mention it.

categories.verdict: No owned channel, no warm capital
categories.reasoning: 9k on X is fine and the 400k-impression launch post got you 200 signups, but that's a moment, not a channel. No warm VC intros means your raise starts cold at exactly the wrong time.

fix_this_first.title: Find out why 9% of clinics leave every month
fix_this_first.why: Every other number in this evaluation improves if this one moves. At 9% you replace your entire customer base in under a year, which makes CAC a subscription rather than an investment.
fix_this_first.do_this: Call every clinic that churned in the last 90 days this week — there are maybe fifteen. Not a survey, a call. Ask what they went back to.

fix_this_first.title: Turn the launch-post audience into a channel
fix_this_first.why: You proved once that you can reach vet operators at scale. Doing it repeatably is cheaper than any paid channel you'd otherwise build.
fix_this_first.do_this: Ship one piece a week aimed at practice managers specifically — claims benchmarks from your own aggregate data is the obvious one and nobody else has it.

fix_this_first.title: Start the raise conversation now, at 7 months
fix_this_first.why: Fundraising takes three to four months and gets measurably harder inside six months of runway, when the ask reads as a rescue rather than a round.
fix_this_first.do_this: Get five warm intros this month through your advisors and the vet-chain network Dana already has.

strategic_notes.title: The claims data is the actual company
strategic_notes.note: Integrations are table stakes and will be copied within a year. What compounds is the reconciliation dataset across thousands of clinics — benchmark pricing, denial rates by insurer. That is a product nobody can start from zero, and it's currently a byproduct you aren't naming.

strategic_notes.title: Multi-location is where pricing breaks
strategic_notes.note: You priced for single clinics but you're selling into 2-8 location groups. At 10x scale, the buyer becomes a procurement conversation with a different sales cycle. Decide now whether you're SMB self-serve or mid-market, because the two need different companies underneath them.

green_flags: A domain founder who actually ran the operation you're selling into
Bottom-up TAM instead of a number lifted from a report
Both founders full-time with revenue already in the door
red_flags: 9% monthly logo churn against 11% growth is net ~2%
7 months of runway with no raise conversation started
No repeatable distribution channel, just one good launch day

research_notes.finding: The seed-stage count is closer to seven, and one of them raised a $9M Series A this year aimed at exactly your 2-8 location segment.
